boards.school_name: California Polytechnic State University-San Luis Obispo
boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Cal Poly spaces for studying, making, exercising, researching, and exploring student-built work, verified through current university and ASI sources.

cards.title: Settle Into the Reopened Kennedy Library
cards.subtitle: Five floors of study space, collaboration rooms, exhibits, and Hub24
cards.notes: Use a collaboration room for group work, browse the first-floor exhibits, or move into Hub24 when you need an overnight study option.
cards.short_summary: A renovated academic hub with individual, collaborative, and round-the-clock study areas.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly reports that Kennedy Library reopened in September 2025 with renovated study areas, two first-floor exhibit spaces, an expanded café, and Hub24 covering the first two floors.
cards.source_title: Light, Spacious and Bustling: Take a Look Inside a Refreshed Kennedy Library
cards.access_notes: Hub24 is identified as the university's 24-hour study space; other library areas follow posted library hours and policies.

cards.entity_name: The Lounge at the University Union
cards.title: Mix Study Time With a Low-Key Break
cards.subtitle: University Union Building 65, Room 119
cards.notes: Bring coursework or a small group, choose indoor or outdoor seating, and use the tabletop games or community library during a break.
cards.short_summary: A student-requested lounge combining study seating, recreation, natural light, and a community library.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI identifies The Lounge as a free-use, 4,176-square-foot campus-community space with study and relaxation areas, indoor and outdoor seating, games, and a community library.
cards.source_title: Discover The Lounge at The University Union
cards.access_notes: Located in Building 65, Room 119. Consult current ASI facility hours before visiting; food from other campus locations may be brought inside.

cards.title: Check the Crowd Before Choosing a Seat
cards.subtitle: A named second-floor lounge inside the University Union
cards.notes: Check ASI's live activity indicator first, then use Chandler Lounge when its posted crowd level suits the kind of work you are doing.
cards.short_summary: A University Union lounge whose current activity level can be checked online before walking over.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI lists Chandler Lounge as a distinct University Union space and publishes a real-time activity indicator accompanied by an interior window-view image.
cards.access_notes: Inside the University Union; entry follows current University Union operating hours and any posted room restrictions.

cards.title: Use the Union's Computer-Ready Lounge
cards.subtitle: A named study lounge inside the University Union
cards.notes: Look at ASI's activity meter before heading over, then use the lounge seating and confirm current computer or printer availability on arrival.
cards.short_summary: A trackable University Union study area previously equipped with library computers and updated printers.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI lists San Luis Lounge as a distinct University Union space with a real-time activity indicator; the University Union page identifies it as one of the building's study lounges.
cards.access_notes: Inside the University Union. Open seating is described by ASI, but current building hours and equipment availability should be checked onsite.

cards.title: Walk Through Five Acres of Student Work
cards.subtitle: A Mediterranean-climate display garden at the end of Via Carta
cards.notes: Follow the self-guided walking tour, examine the labeled plant collections, and notice the class and senior projects incorporated into the garden.
cards.short_summary: A free campus garden designed, built, and maintained through student learning projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly describes the five-acre Leaning Pine Arboretum as a year-round campus garden whose features were designed, built, and maintained by students through classes, labs, and senior projects.
cards.access_notes: The university lists public hours as 8 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Saturday, excluding academic holidays; visitors should remain on permitted paths.

cards.title: See Full-Scale Design Experiments in Poly Canyon
cards.subtitle: The nine-acre outdoor laboratory commonly associated with the Architecture Graveyard
cards.notes: Visit in daylight to observe student-built structures at full scale, stay on established routes, and follow every posted site restriction.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor CAED laboratory holding decades of large-scale student-designed structures.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly identifies the Experimental Practices Laboratory in Poly Canyon as a nine-acre outdoor laboratory containing large-scale structures designed and built by students since 1964.
cards.access_notes: This is an academic outdoor laboratory. Visit only during permitted daylight access, use established routes, and do not enter or climb structures.

cards.title: Handle Real Materials While Researching Design
cards.subtitle: Architecture Building 05, Room 101
cards.notes: Pair book or image research with the materials collection, then ask staff for help refining searches tied to architecture or environmental design.
cards.short_summary: A CAED study room combining specialized publications, digital images, drawings, and thousands of material samples.
cards.evidence_claim: The Neel Resource Center provides study, research, and browsing space plus architecture and environmental-design collections, including about 7,000 hands-on material samples.
cards.source_title: About Us - Paul & Verla Neel Resource Center
cards.access_notes: Located in Building 05, Room 101. The center directs visitors to contact CAED for current hours; collection circulation rules vary by material.

cards.title: Study a Living Collection Under Glass
cards.subtitle: A central-campus glasshouse supporting plant teaching and research
cards.notes: Examine the labeled living collection as a visual reference for plant coursework, and verify public access or class use before entering the glasshouse.
cards.short_summary: A campus glasshouse organized as a living museum for Cal Poly teaching and research.
cards.evidence_claim: Cal Poly describes the Plant Conservatory as a large central-campus glasshouse maintaining a diverse, documented, and labeled living collection for student and faculty teaching and research.
cards.access_notes: The official page establishes its academic purpose but does not state unrestricted public entry; verify current access before visiting.

cards.title: Choose a Workout Space That Fits the Day
cards.subtitle: Building 43 fitness, recreation, and relaxation facilities
cards.notes: Check current hours and space activity, then choose among exercise rooms, courts, the indoor track, pools, or another available recreation area.
cards.short_summary: A student-shaped recreation complex with indoor, outdoor, aquatic, and relaxation facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI says the Recreation Center serves students and the campus community with exercise rooms, an indoor track, six gym courts, racquetball courts, pools, volleyball courts, and a climbing park.
cards.access_notes: Access requires an eligible membership or guest pass. Check current ASI hours, activity levels, reservations, and temporary closures before arrival.

cards.title: Make Something in a Shared Studio
cards.subtitle: Student-focused studios ranging from fiber arts to surfboard shaping
cards.notes: Review the studio choices and eligibility rules, then register or obtain any required access before bringing a project into the appropriate workspace.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on creative facility where students can learn techniques and work across several craft studios.
cards.evidence_claim: ASI describes the Craft Center as a place to connect, relax, and make projects in studios spanning activities such as surfboard shaping and fiber arts.
cards.access_notes: Programs are designed for Cal Poly students and may require fees, registration, or studio authorization. The center can close during summer; verify current hours.
